title: The interview
text:
Maja had never felt so nervous. It was the morning of her first real job interview, at a design company in the centre of Kraków. She had prepared for days: she had read everything about the company, practised her answers with her flatmate and ironed her best white shirt.

She left home early, but when she was waiting at the tram stop, it started to rain heavily. She didn't have an umbrella. By the time the tram arrived, her hair was wet and her white shirt was not so white any more – a passing car had splashed muddy water all over her.

Maja almost went home. "They'll never give me the job now," she thought. But then she remembered something her grandmother always said: "People remember how you behave, not how you look." So she took a deep breath and went to the interview.

The receptionist looked at her with surprise and gave her a towel and a cup of tea. When Maja walked into the meeting room, she smiled and said, "I'm sorry about my appearance. Let's just say the weather didn't want me to get this job." The three people on the other side of the table laughed.

The interview went better than she had expected. She talked about her ideas, showed her portfolio and asked good questions. At the end, the manager shook her hand. "Anyone who can stay calm after a morning like that," he said, "can deal with our clients."

A week later, Maja got an email. She had the job. On her first day, she brought an umbrella – and a spare shirt.
